Dine with a noble cause & enjoy authentic Vietnamese cuisine in a lovely setting
Sep 2025 • Friends
This is the place to go for authentic Vietnamese cuisine in a lovely French colonial setting. We had the grilled chicken with lemon leaves (ga nuong la chanh), purple yam soup (canh khoai mo), beancurd with mushrooms & stir fried morning glory with garlic. All of them were really tasty, but the grilled chicken was exceptional. Service was good and staff were friendly & welcoming. The restaurant supports a good cause by training and employing disadvantaged youths too.

Great food and helping a social cause
Feb 2020
Huong Lai is a little hard to find. It's on the first floor of a nondescript building and you probably will miss it if you aren't looking for. That's a pity for the food was the best I tasted in HCMC, and the price was amongst the cheapest. The wait staff are all street kids who clearly appreciate the opportunity the restaurant is providing them and are cheerful and helpful. All were relatively fluent in English. The restaurant itself is nothing special in terms of décor and the elderly air con will no doubt struggle with summer temperatures but the food and fast service make up for this. Recommended..

A special New Years meal
Dec 2019 • Couples
We dined here on New Years Eve and we weren’t disappointed. The restaurant is low key from the outside, then as you make your way up the stairs (definitely not recommended for the elderly or infirm) you enter a quaint dining room. The staff greeting us on arrival were so friendly, with impeccable manners, it would be hard not to be impressed. The concept of the restaurant is beautiful too, in that it trains and employs orphans and those from disadvantaged backgrounds.

We elected to order the Seafood Set Menu ($280,000 VND pp) and whilst the food was very good, it’s the staff that truly make the experience. We were served by a number of wait staff and nothing was too much trouble. I’d like to single out Hoa for her beautiful service and thank all of the staff present on New Years Eve for a wonderful evening. All the best for the New Year and may all your dreams come true in 2020 ❤️

Delicious dinner and relaxed vibe
Dec 2019 • Couples
We loved our dinner visit to the lovely Huong Lai restaurant, a 15min level stroll from our riverside hotel.
A staircase leads up to the 1st-floor dining area; modest tables and decor, busy, buzzy, 1940s music, friendly, fans, jasmine flowers on the tables. Unpretentious and all the better for that methinks.
After a shared starter, we chose fried chicken in tamarind hentic. Relaxed too. Time to savour our meal, served by the very friendly, "natural" staff. 
I'd really recommend dinner here, and the walk means you are again exposed to the hectic pace of this fabulous, friendly city.
Enjoy!

Charming place, pretty good food
Dec 2019 • Family
Just off busy Dong Khoi Street sits a nondescript building with a small brightly-lit sign marking the entrance to Huong Lai. Entering the first floor of a narrow building, you ascend an impossibly steep stairway to reveal a romantic and charming dining room. The customers are predominantly locals, but a tourist or two manages to find this place. Making reservations is highly recommended, but they managed to squeeze us in without making one. However, by the time we left, they were booked for the night and we would have been out of luck.

The wonderful premise of this restaurant is that they mostly employee orphans and impoverished individuals, young people who exude so much charm and manners you’d never know they had overcome personal struggle. The restaurant is a training ground for their English speaking and interpersonal skills and that made it worth my money! The prices are also incredibly reasonable.

I started with fried spring rolls, certainly not the best in Ho Chi Minh City, but very good. The accompanying sauce isn’t as potent and spicy as it should be, but it will suffice.

I had the Fried Chicken with Spicy Sauce as my entree. You have to eat around the bones, which is a bit cumbersome, but this gives the dish good flavor. It’s not deep fried like a tempura, but closer to grilled and slightly crispy than anything. The dish was tasty with delicious vegetables.
